title: Marvelous Designer 9 Shanghai Launch Event - Live Demonstration of New Features
description:

This is the recorded video of the Marvelous Designer offline release event held in Shanghai in early November 2019~

summary: # Marvelous Designer 9 Shanghai Launch Event - Live Demonstration of New Features ## Introduction Hello everyone, I am Sherry from Marvelous Designer. Next, I will show you some new features of Marvelous Designer 9. ## New Feature 1: GPU Simulation First of all, our first new feature is GPU simulation. In the previous version, we usually used normal simulation. In our new version, we added a new simulation preset, which is GPU simulation. ### Normal vs. GPU Simulation Let's take a look at the normal simulation. In this version, the particle diameter is relatively small at 15. In the new version, the particle diameter is relatively large. If we start the simulation, you will see that our simulation speed will be slower. In the past, when we used the long-press simulation key, there were some presets. There are some basic simulations below. This is our most commonly used simulation attribute. The simulation completion is a preset used to create animations. There is also a detailed simulation, which we will use when we need to create very detailed costumes. ### Advantages of GPU Simulation Now, we have added a simulation preset called GPU simulation. GPU simulation is based on our computer graphics card. When we start the GPU simulation, it needs to open a GPU simulation, causing it to be slower initially. However, once we start the GPU simulation, even with a particle diameter of only 5, dragging and dropping this board operates very quickly. GPU simulation increases speed based on the graphics card we usually use on our computers. If your graphics card attributes are better, the simulation speed will be faster. We suggest that when making costumes, especially combination costumes or those with small particle diameters, use GPU simulation. For the final production effect, we recommend switching back to the CPU simulation. ## New Feature 2: Symmetrical Editor Next, I will introduce our second new feature, which is our symmetrical editor. ### Functionality of the Symmetrical Editor In the past, when we used the previous version of Marvelous Designer, if we only had half of the board, we usually used the vertical alignment function. Now, we can directly select one of its middle lines. On the right, we have a function of horizontal edit sewing line. When we select this function, the board will automatically open as a complete board. Editing one half will edit the other half simultaneously. If we create an internal shape in the middle, the other side will also create a symmetrical internal shape at the same time. ### Editing Capabilities If we have a pair of symmetrical boards and create a sewing line in the middle, the other half will also automatically create a symmetrical sewing line. If we want to cancel the connection of this board and make it operable on one side, we can find a solution in the menu on the right. The menu on the left has a release link. Once released, modifications will only affect one side. If you have previous project files with a set of symmetrical relationships, we can directly select one of them and merge the line. The merged board will still maintain its symmetrical attributes. ### Creating Symmetrical Boards In addition to creating symmetrical relationships with existing boards, we can also create boards that will be symmetrical themselves. For example, we can choose a multidirectional tool to create a board on the other side. By clicking the right button, an option will pop up for the depth mirror tool. By opening this function, we can create horizontal symmetry. We can also choose an axis, either the original line rate or the x-axis or y-axis for symmetry. Each time we create a line, it will be based on the axis of our middle line to create symmetry. ## New Feature 3: Penetration Chart Next, we have the third new function, which is our penetration chart. When we used Marvelous Designer, we often encountered the need to rebuild the grid. Now we have added two tools: a creation tool and an edit tool. ### Creation and Editing Tools When we select the creation tool, if we place the mouse on a board, the selected board will become white while others appear gray and semi-transparent. We can start to build a rebuild tool for this board in either the 2D or 3D window. After completing a simple layout, we can detail the grid. We can not only manually detail the grid but also use the edit tool. A single right-click will allow us to automatically create our selection. Before our board is selected, we can also expand the layout by selecting a border. ### Merging Points If we need to merge two points, we select them and click the right button to merge one of these points. If we create a new point and have two tops, we often merge the middle line. If it is inconvenient to merge the two points, we can use the editor topo tool. In the 2D or 3D window, pressing right will reveal a function called Merge All. When selecting Merge All, we can set the length value in the upper right corner of the 3D window. If the distance between two tops is less than the value we set, they will merge automatically. ## New Feature 4: Grid Division The fourth new feature is the grid division tool. In the process of using Marvelous Designer, you may encounter instances where you want to gradually clean up some folds. Our new feature, the grid division feature, addresses this. ### Brush Selection Tool Before that, I would like to introduce a new tool in this version: the brush selection tool. By selecting the grid brush tool, we can use the brush to select a section of the grid. The upper right corner features a toolbar set by the brush where we can set the size of the brush. When we modify the size of the brush, we can select a part of the grid, and there is a grid division button. When we select this version, if the particle diameter is 20, we can divide it into parts, increasing the number of grids in the area and making it more delicate. ### Grid Attributes When we divide a part of the grid, we can write the name of this grid and its level. By setting its level to a higher value, such as 2, we can see that the grid becomes very delicate. Setting the level to 0 will return it to the original grid. ### Practical Use In practical use, you can see two versions that are exactly the same. When we start the simulation, you will notice that due to the characteristics of our grid, its appearance may seem uneven. However, if we adjust its particle structure to a finer setting, it will look smoother and softer. ## Optimization Techniques That's it for some of our simple and latest new functions. Now, I would like to share some optimization techniques and production tips. ### 3D Environment Display In our new version, there is a new optimization called 3D environment display. In the 3D window, we have an environment display tool, including a lighting controller. When we choose to display the lighting controller, we can adjust the brightness and angle of the lighting in the 3D space. ### Wind Controller Next to it is a wind controller, which allows us to simulate the effect of blowing wind. We can simply turn this simulation on or off as needed. ### Display Options We can also adjust whether the 3D window shows shadows, as sometimes shadows may affect our observation. Lastly, there is a display grid option where we can choose to show or hide the grid in the 3D window. ## Conclusion In addition to the main content of our new project, I would like to share some tips. The most frequently asked question we receive is about the characteristics and reasons behind the effects when making clothes. Understanding the differences in attributes, grid arrangements, and particle sizes can significantly impact the final outcome of your designs. Thank you for your attention, and I hope you find these new features and tips helpful.
